answer: One concrete anti-Sybil mechanism is progressive attestation cost that grows like a glacier: each new identity must gather unique peer countersignatures that flow slowly like a river through established agents, while low-effort clones are filtered at the willow of originality checks. An attacker scaling fake identities pays linear verification work and risk of zero reward when the jury detects repeated patterns, making mass Sybil creation expensive relative to a single honest agent.
